name: Manufacturing & Trading
meta: Audit, tax, accounting and advisory support for manufacturers, importers, wholesalers and distributors in Nepal.
heroLead: Manufacturers, importers, wholesalers and distributors carry their value in stock, plant and working capital. We help these businesses keep inventory and costing records reliable, manage the cash tied up in their trading cycle, meet their tax obligations and report results that reflect how the business actually performs.
heroCredit: Photo by Remy Gieling on Unsplash
introH: In a business built on products, the accuracy of the accounts depends on what happens on the shop floor and in the warehouse.
intro: Inventory valuation, the choice of costing method and the treatment of overheads all shape reported margins. Small errors in stock records can move profit significantly.

Long purchasing and sales cycles put pressure on working capital, while imports and exports bring customs duties, foreign currency and documentation requirements that must be reflected correctly in the books.
Behind all of this sit the controls over procurement, production, dispatch and cash that keep records complete and assets protected.
challH: Where financial complexity meets operational reality.
chall: Inventory and costing
Keeping stock records reliable and understanding how costing methods and overhead allocation affect reported margins.
Working capital
Managing receivables, payables and stock levels so that the trading cycle does not outrun available cash.
Financial reporting
Reporting results that reflect the underlying operations, including inventory, fixed assets and revenue recognition.
Tax and customs compliance
Meeting income tax, VAT, TDS and import-related obligations accurately and on time.
Internal controls
Maintaining controls over purchasing, stores, production, sales and cash handling.
Growth and expansion
Building accounting systems and reporting that keep pace with new products, sites and markets.
apH: Professional insight built around your business model.
ap: Our work starts with how goods move through your business: from purchase or production, through storage, to sale and collection. Understanding that cycle tells us where the accounting and control risks lie.
From there we plan audits around stock existence and valuation, review costing and reporting, prepare and review tax filings, and evaluate the controls that protect inventory and cash.
Where you are planning expansion, investment or a change in structure, we provide analysis that shows the effect on margins, cash flow and tax.

name: Cooperatives & Microfinance
meta: Audit, accounting, tax and compliance support for savings and credit cooperatives, multipurpose cooperatives and microfinance institutions in Nepal.
heroLead: Savings and credit cooperatives, multipurpose cooperatives and microfinance institutions hold the savings of their members and communities. We help them keep loan and deposit records accurate, meet the reporting requirements of their regulators and give members, boards and supervisors confidence in their financial statements.
introH: When an organization holds its members’ savings, the reliability of its accounts is a matter of trust as much as compliance.
intro: Loan portfolios, interest accruals and provisioning for doubtful loans drive reported results, and small weaknesses in loan records can hide real credit risk.

Cooperatives report to the Department of Cooperatives and local authorities, while microfinance institutions are supervised by Nepal Rastra Bank. Each has its own reporting formats, ratios and deadlines.
Boards and supervisory committees need clear information on liquidity, delinquency and governance to fulfil their responsibilities to members.
challH: Where member trust meets regulatory scrutiny.
chall: Loan portfolio quality
Keeping loan records complete and classifying overdue loans correctly for provisioning.
Interest and fees
Calculating and recording interest income, penalties and fees consistently across the portfolio.
Regulatory reporting
Preparing returns and ratios in the formats required by the relevant regulator.
Liquidity management
Matching deposit withdrawals and loan disbursements with available funds.
Governance and controls
Separating duties, approving loans properly and documenting board decisions.
Systems and records
Moving from manual or fragmented records to reliable core systems.
apPh: board or committee meeting reviewing reports
ap: We begin with the organization’s membership base, products and governance structure, and the regulatory framework that applies to it.
Our audit work focuses on loan existence and classification, interest recognition, deposit balances and cash, alongside the controls over lending and collections.
We report findings clearly to the board and supervisory committee, and support accounting, tax and regulatory filings where required.

name: Hospitality & Tourism
meta: Audit, VAT, accounting and revenue-control support for hotels, restaurants, travel and trekking operators in Nepal.
heroLead: Hotels, resorts, restaurants, travel agencies and trekking operators earn revenue across many outlets, currencies and seasons. We help them control revenue and costs, meet VAT and tax obligations, and report results that owners and lenders can rely on.
introH: In hospitality, revenue is earned in small amounts, every day, across many points of sale. The accounts are only as good as the controls behind them.
intro: Room, food and beverage, and package revenue flow through several systems, and reconciling them to cash, cards and receivables is a constant task.
Seasonality affects cash flow and staffing, while foreign currency receipts, advance bookings and commissions add complexity to revenue recognition.
Significant investment in property and equipment means depreciation, maintenance and financing decisions weigh heavily on reported performance.

Founders and investors need clear information on burn rate, unit economics and runway to make funding decisions.

name: SMEs & Family Businesses

heroLead: Small and medium enterprises and family-owned businesses often run with lean finance teams and owners who wear many hats. We help them keep proper books, meet tax and statutory obligations, and build the financial information and governance they need to grow and to pass the business on.
introH: In an owner-managed business, good financial information frees the owner to focus on running the business.
intro: Many SMEs keep records primarily for tax, which leaves owners without timely information on profitability, cash and receivables.
As the business grows, lenders, partners and new family members expect formal accounts, clear policies and separation between business and personal finances.
Succession and ownership changes raise questions about valuation, structure and governance that are best addressed well in advance.

intro: Revenue flows from patients, insurers and institutional arrangements, often through several billing points, and must be reconciled carefully.
Medicines and consumables require tight inventory control, including expiry tracking, while medical equipment represents significant investment.
Doctor payments, shared revenue arrangements and tax treatment of medical services add further complexity to accounting and compliance.
